easy.def: A set of events that repeat.

more.def: A series of events that happen again and again in the same order.
examples: The water cycle moves water from the sea to the sky and back.
The seasons form a cycle each year.
The washing machine finished its cycle.
I cycle to school every day.
She cycled to the library on her new bike.

easy.def: A person who rides a bike.

more.def: A person who rides a bicycle.
examples: The cyclist wore a helmet and rode along the bike path.
A cyclist raced up the hill.
The cyclists rode in a long line.

easy.def: A strong wind that spins in a circle.

more.def: A large storm with strong winds that spin around a center.
examples: A cyclone hit the island with heavy rain.
The cyclone tore branches from the trees.
The village prepared for the cyclone.
A gray cygnet followed its mother across the pond.
A cygnet grows into a white swan.

easy.def: A shape like a can, with flat round ends.

more.def: A shape with straight sides and two flat, round ends of the same size, like a can or a tube.
examples: A soup can is shaped like a cylinder.
The teacher held up a cylinder and asked us to count its flat faces.
Each of the tall candles was a perfect cylinder.

easy.def: Shaped like a tube or can.

more.def: Shaped like a cylinder, with round, flat ends and straight sides.
examples: A cylindrical tower stood by the castle.
The pipe was long and cylindrical.

easy.def: Two round metal plates that you crash together.

more.def: Two round metal plates that are struck together to make a ringing sound.
examples: The cymbals made a loud ringing sound.
She played the cymbals in the band.

easy.def: A tall, dark tree that stays green.

more.def: A tall evergreen tree with dark green leaves, often found in warm places.
examples: Tall cypresses lined the road to the villa.
The cypress grows in swamps and warm hills.
A cypress tree stood in the old garden.
